title: Autoscaling by metric, by schedule and by prediction

videos.script: A fixed number of machines is wrong twice a day. This lesson replaces the number with a rule. {{target}} The commonest rule is a CPU target. Add up how busy the machines are, divide by the target, round up. You will do that sum yourself. {{signals}} Some services wait more than they compute. For them the signal is the load balancer, or the length of a queue, which can take a worker down to zero. {{schedule}} Some load is known in advance. A schedule raises the floor before nine o'clock, and costs a little money every morning. {{predict}} And some load repeats. Prediction learns it from three days of history. {{slow}} Last, the way down. The group shrinks slowly on purpose, because the load that just left often comes straight back.
